content.user_title: Design Email Preference and Frequency Controls
content.value_statement: Subscribers may leave when email topics or frequency do not fit their needs. This skill designs clear controls and maps every choice to an enforceable rule.
actual_capabilities: Defines preference-center fields for topics, cadence tiers, channel controls, and confirmation behavior.
Designs ordered opt-down steps before a complete unsubscribe.
Maps each subscriber choice to a suppression or frequency rule.
Defines pause windows and the sunset condition that ends the ladder.
Produces a SEND N sub-item assessment with Pass, Partial, or Fail rationale.
limitations: Does not implement settings inside an email service provider.
Does not store the authoritative consent or suppression record.
Does not design complete lifecycle flows or global send governance.
Does not calculate the full Email Quality Score or decide the N1 veto.

use_cases.title: Reduce Unsubscribe Pressure
use_cases.description: Create topic, cadence, and pause choices for a marketing program with rising opt-out rates.

use_cases.title: Specify Preference Rules
use_cases.description: Translate subscriber-facing controls into clear suppression and frequency requirements for implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Preference Coverage
use_cases.description: Assess whether an existing preference center provides usable alternatives while keeping complete unsubscribe accessible.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Preference Center
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preference center for [audience] on [platform]. Include topics [list], weekly and monthly options, a pause, and complete unsubscribe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with known topics and simple cadence choices.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Opt-Down Ladder
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ordered opt-down ladder for [program]. Offer reduced frequency, topic selection, a [duration] pause, and an accessible complete unsubscribe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reduce avoidable unsubscribes without obstructing user choice.

prompt_templates.title: Map Choices to Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Map every control in this preference-center description to explicit suppression, frequency, pause, resume, and sunset rules: [description].
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare requirements for an email platform and consent registry.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Redesign Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this preference export and opt-out flow: [details]. Label evidence sources, identify gaps, redesign the ladder, map rules, and assess the SEND N sub-item.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced evidence-based review of an existing program.

output_examples.input: A weekly product newsletter needs topic controls, monthly delivery, and a 90-day pause.
output: Topics: product updates, tutorials, and events can be muted independently.
Cadence: weekly, monthly, or paused for 90 days.
Complete unsubscribe remains available in one step.

output_examples.input: Map a monthly choice and a 60-day pause to operational rules.
output_examples.output: Monthly limits delivery to one eligible message each month. Pause suppresses eligible sends for 60 days, then restores the prior cadence.

output_examples.input: Assess a page that offers only a complete unsubscribe and no preference options.
output_examples.output: SEND N sub-item: Fail. The page provides no topic, cadence, or pause alternative, although the complete unsubscribe path remains available.

best_practices: Use a small set of distinct topics that match real message streams.
Offer only cadence tiers that the delivery system can enforce.
Keep complete unsubscribe visible, direct, and available in one step.
anti_patterns: Do not hide or delay complete unsubscribe behind preference choices.
Do not offer topic controls that suppress unrelated message streams.
Do not promise cadence limits that lifecycle flows cannot honor.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, message topics, current cadence, email platform, and existing opt-out flow when available.

faq.question: Can this skill implement the preference center?
faq.answer: No. It creates the field, ladder, and rule specification for implementation in your platform.

faq.question: Does it replace a consent registry?
faq.answer: No. It defines mappings, while the consent registry remains the authoritative record for consent and suppression.

faq.question: Will it prevent complete unsubscribes?
faq.answer: No. It offers voluntary alternatives while requiring complete unsubscribe to remain direct and accessible.

faq.question: Can it work without an export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use stated topics and cadence tiers, but current-state conclusions will be limited.

faq.question: Does it calculate a full email quality score?
faq.answer: No. It produces one SEND N sub-item assessment for a separate auditor to include.
